🇲🇽🎓 MEXICO CITY MAKES UNIVERSITY TRANSPORT A SOCIAL RIGHT

Mexico City Head of Government Clara Brugada launched a University Transport Scholarship: 1,500 pesos every two months for public-university students, with no grade average or income test. The city has already handed out 72,443 cards and targets 200,000 by year's end. "The objective is that no young person abandons their studies due to lack of economic resources," Brugada said.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO BLACKLISTS TWO FIRMS THAT FAKED HEALTH-CONTRACT PAPERWORK

Mexico's Anticorruption and Good Government Ministry, through IMSS internal control, sanctioned two companies over federal health contracts: Alta Especialidad de Medicina y Capacitación was fined 138,911 pesos and barred for 15 months for submitting false information on an ambulance contract, while Protein SA was fined the same amount and barred for failing to deliver 150 units of chloroquine. Both now sit in the public registry of sanctioned contractors, locked out of federal bidding.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 MEXICO CITY MARCHES FOR CUBA AS WASHINGTON ESCALATES ITS THREATS

Civil organizations will march in Mexico City on July 26, from the Hemiciclo a Juárez to the former U.S. Embassy, under the banner "No a la guerra contra Cuba" — a response to the July 20 State Department report branding the island "the capital of 21st-century communism" and accusing it of a "war of attrition" against the U.S. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez called it a pretext for "a cruel and criminal economic war that punishes every Cuban family."

🇲🇽⛏️ THE IEA ENDORSES MEXICO'S SOVEREIGN CONTROL OVER ITS CRITICAL MINERALS

The International Energy Agency says Mexico's new critical-minerals framework "fosters the generation and retention of value" both nationally and across North America, praising its treatment of these resources as "strategic and sovereign" with stricter environmental and social standards. Lithium was nationalized by decree in 2022, with exploration and extraction reserved exclusively to the Mexican state through LitioMx.

🇲🇽🐢 MEXICO REVOKES DEVELOPER'S BEACH CONCESSION TO PROTECT SEA-TURTLE NESTING GROUND

Mexico's environment ministry (Semarnat) revoked the federal beach concession of developer Cantiles de Mita, which had been clearing critical nesting habitat for leatherback, olive ridley and hawksbill turtles at Playa Las Cocinas, Nayarit, to build luxury housing without authorization. Secretary Alicia Bárcena canceled it for "non-compliance" after a technical, legal and administrative review.

🇲🇽⚽ "Mexico was the best host of the three." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 21 Of the 2026 World Cup's three host nations — Mexico, the US and Canada — Sheinbaum said Mexico was by far the best venue. A full report and recognition for the security teams come next week.

🇲🇽🔍 Asked if Washington would use the "El Mayo" sentence to pressure Mexico on security, Sheinbaum said no. "It's the work we're doing ourselves, on the principle of attention to the root causes." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 21 After Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada's US sentencing, Sheinbaum ruled out that the case would become a lever for US pressure. Mexico keeps its own strategy — addressing the social roots of violence, not just repression.

🇲🇽✊ "We're expanding services where they never existed — or where years of disinvestment left the IMSS completely insufficient." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS director general, mañanera, July 21 47 IMSS hospitals in the plan: 7 already operating, 21 under construction — including 553-bed and 558-bed hospitals in Nuevo León and Coahuila. Robledo framed it as repairing decades of neoliberal underinvestment.
